text:
Noah Dobson has played 21 games for Montreal this season without a goal. Dose.ca's headline puts the drought at "55 games without a goal (and it's starting to become a problem)," and Sportsnet wrote that the Canadiens need to "get more from Dobson."

Our numbers are kinder than the headlines. He has 3.0 expected goals (the quality of his chances) and zero goals, and Montreal has scored 7.2 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice. That reads as due: he keeps getting looks, and goals tend to follow chances. At five on five the Canadiens take 52.3% of the expected goals with him out there, 3.2 points better than without him, and he has 9 assists while averaging 21 minutes.

The worry is the shot itself. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him attempting 6.9 shots per 60 last season, 81st percentile, but fewer from the slot than that volume suggests. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.16 more expected goals per 60 with him on the ice, bottom 5% of defensemen, against tough competition.

Watch whether he starts getting inside. The luck should turn; the location is up to him.
